analysis.title: Rates Outlook 2027: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly
key_insights: ING's baseline has the US 10yr Treasury yield rising to about 5.25% in early 2027 (vs 4.9% currently), with a possible peak of 5.5%, before falling to 4.5-4.75% later in 2027 as inflation eases.

Three forces drive long-end rates: the 'good' of AI-driven productivity, the 'bad' of elevated fiscal deficits, and the 'ugly' of renewed inflation from ongoing wars. ING says AI's share of the move is about a fifth, but AI-related issuance is a growing factor.

ING says the February 2026 bond sell-off was sparked by the Iran war via elevated printed inflation. Inflation falling later in 2027 would let the Fed step away and the market re-discount cuts, which pulls long yields lower.

ING expects US swap spreads to re-widen through 2027 or at least Q1. It sees the 10yr swap spread going from below 40bp to 50bp-plus and the 30yr to 75bp at least, and prefers to fade the recent tightening.
Swap spreads have tightened partly because of Bessent's increase in long-end buybacks and fast-money players going long Treasuries and paying in swaps against an implied cap on spreads.

ING sees three routes to a 6% US 10yr, none in its baseline: GDP growth of 3-4% pushing the real yield toward 4%, the deficit rising from 6-6.5% to 7-8% of GDP, or inflation stuck near 3% or worse (e.g. a severe El Niño).
A material cut in long-end Treasury issuance is the main wildcard that would lower yields. ING does not expect it outside market stress.

Euro rates face a bumpy start to 2027, with markets reacting to each inflation print for signs of second-round effects. In the baseline the 2yr EUR swap rate falls about 50bp. In the bad case the 10yr swap rate goes well above 4%, and in the fast-disinflation case it goes toward 2%.
ING's baseline has oil below $80/bbl and the ECB terminal rate near 2.5% by end-2027. It argues markets have over-repriced the terminal rate above 3%, against the earlier 1.75-2.25% range.

The 10yr euro swap is sticky because global real rates and bond supply, including QT, push long yields up. ING judges it close to fair value at nominal growth expectations of about 3.3%, which limits the downside.

Market pricing implies about three more ECB hikes with the 1Y1Y inflation forward at 2.2% and 5y5y inflation swaps at 2.1%. ING calls an ECB forced to tolerate higher inflation an unpriced tail risk that would steepen curves significantly.
A perceived weakening of monetary policy transmission plus upside inflation surprises could push 2yr euro swap rates another 100bp higher.

France is the key fault line. ING sees a 10yr OAT-Bund spread of about 150bp as a floor during electoral uncertainty, with a tail beyond 200bp if Mélenchon's platform gains probability. The 2027 presidential election rounds are 18 April and 2 May.

Moody's affirmed France's AA rating with a negative outlook, and Fitch lowered the outlook on France's A+ rating to negative. ING says the market prices French debt as if rated BBB, wider than fundamentals imply.

ING expects the ECB to let French spreads play out while the turmoil stays contained. Its options are, in order, a less hawkish stance, ending QT, then the TPI. ING sees a high bar for intervention (the 2011 SMP came at BTP-Bund spreads above 500bp).

Bunds are in a temporary safe-haven bid. ING expects the 10yr Bund to cheapen from about 13bp to at least 20bp over OIS as German gross issuance could exceed €400bn next year, about €50bn more than this year, with about €80bn more from ECB runoff.

ING sees sterling rates falling in 2027 but only late: the BoE must show inflation heading to target by end-2027, and the market's pricing of at least 100bp more hikes (terminal about 4.75%) is seen as excessive and a legacy of past trading losses.

The 10yr GBP swap rate is explained about 98% by BoE expectations and the US swap curve (10yr level and 2s10s slope). Gilt supply is going to price-sensitive buyers, which keeps a term premium in place and makes the path lower volatile.

Dutch pension reform: about €600bn has transitioned in 2026 and over €900bn is set for January 2027. ING expects limited immediate impact thanks to funding ratios above 105% (ABP above 130%) but a structurally steeper 10s30s euro curve and more frequent swap rebalancing tied to equity prices.

macro_indicators.interpretation: ING expects yields to rise further in the near term on AI, deficits and inflation before easing as inflation falls and Fed cuts are repriced.

Stable but not improving. A move to 7-8% is one of the three routes to a 6% 10yr.

Little priced risk to the ECB's 2% commitment.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Safe-haven premium fades and supply pressure returns.

trade_ideas.description: Fade tight US swap spreads: position for the 10yr swap spread to widen from below 40bp to 50bp-plus and the 30yr to 75bp
trade_ideas.rationale: ING expects re-widening pressure through 2027, or at least Q1, as the fiscal deficit narrative persists.
trade_ideas.risk: Treasury cancels some long-end auctions or adds to buybacks.

trade_ideas.description: Avoid positioning bond-bullish early in 2027 on US Treasuries
trade_ideas.rationale: ING sees yields pushing to 5.25-5.5% in Q1 before inflation eases and cuts are repriced.
trade_ideas.risk: A material cut in long-end Treasury issuance.

risk_factors: Inflation failing to ease enough, which would keep central banks hawkish and bond markets without relief.
Three routes to a 6% US 10yr: 3-4% GDP growth, a deficit of 7-8%, or inflation stuck near 3% or worse.
AI-related debt issuance crowding out AI productivity gains in the effect on yields.
French political and fiscal risk, including downgrades and possible foreign investor exit.
An ECB forced to tolerate higher inflation, which would steepen curves.
Rising private-sector and non-US government bond issuance.
A weakening of monetary policy transmission combined with inflation surprises, which could add 100bp to the 2yr euro swap rate.
US inflation persistence spilling over to sterling via a 10yr USD swap near 6%.
vol_and_positioning: Fast-money players are long Treasuries and paying in swaps against an implied cap on swap spreads, which tightened US swap spreads. ING prefers to fade this.
Gilt supply is being absorbed by price-sensitive buyers (foreign investors, asset managers, hedge funds), which can bring volatility.
Dutch pension funds will rebalance swap hedges more often as hedging ties to asset prices.
geopolitical: The Iran war sparked the February 2026 bond sell-off through elevated inflation, and ongoing wars keep inflation pressure on.
Middle East turmoil tied sovereign spreads to energy prices and ECB hike expectations.
France's 2027 presidential election (18 April and 2 May), with the possibility of snap legislative elections in summer.
Spain votes later this month, Italy must hold legislative elections before the end of next year, Finland holds parliamentary elections, and Germany has five state elections, four in April and May.
Possible US Treasury steps on long-end issuance or buybacks.

tension_points.bull_case: Inflation, GDP and the deficit stabilise, the Fed steps away and cuts are repriced, taking the 10yr to 4.5-4.75% later in 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Inflation stays near 3%, growth reaches 3-4% or the deficit goes to 7-8%, each a route to a 6% 10yr.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation not easing enough to comfort central banks, or the deficit rising to 7-8% of GDP.

tension_points.bull_case: Benign inflation readings let the 2yr EUR swap fall about 50bp and the ECB terminal rate settle near 2.5%.
tension_points.bear_case: One bad inflation reading risks a repeat of 2022-23, and a weakened ECB transmission could add 100bp to the 2yr swap and push the 10yr well above 4%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A series of upside inflation surprises, or evidence of second-round effects.

tension_points.bull_case: A Le Pen win with credible consolidation could bring spreads back toward pre-September levels.
tension_points.bear_case: Unrealistic consolidation plans, a hung parliament or Mélenchon support could push the OAT-Bund spread beyond 200bp.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A credible multi-year French fiscal consolidation plan after the April and May 2027 elections.
